name: Question 1
worked_solution:
First, we let $f(y)=2{y}^{2}-8y+26.$

Next, we solve $f(y)=0$ by completing the square, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(y) & =0 \\ 2{y}^{2}-8y+26 & =0 \\ {y}^{2}-4y+13 & =0 \\ ({y}^{2}-2\cdot 2\cdot y+{2}^{2})-{2}^{2}+13 & =0 \\ (y-2)^{2}-4+13 & =0 \\ (y-2)^{2}+9 & =0 \\ (y-2)^{2} & =-9 \\ (y-2)^{2} & =9{\text{i}}^{2} \\ (y-2)^{2} & ={(3\text{i})}^{2} \\ y-2 & =\pm 3\text{i} \\ y & =2\pm 3\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since our quadratic equation has roots ${y}_{1}=2+3\text{i}$ and ${y}_{2}=2-3\text{i},$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=2,$ the expression $2{y}^{2}-8y+26$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}2{y}^{2}-8y+26 & =a(y-{y}_{1})(y-{y}_{2}) \\  & =2(y-(2+3\text{i}))(y-(2-3\text{i})).\end{aligned}
$$
